title: Leg angiogram
what: The doctor passes a thin tube into an artery and injects contrast dye. X-rays show where the leg arteries are narrowed. Sometimes they are widened during the same procedure.
why: For leg pain when walking, slow-healing wounds on the feet, or if an ultrasound showed narrowed arteries.
duration: the procedure usually takes 30 to 90 minutes, followed by a few hours of bed rest; usually up to 1 to 2 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners and diabetes medicines. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergy to iodine or contrast dye

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, including kidney function, and an ECG. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for a few hours before. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Skin prep
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked to shave the groin. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, your daily medicines, and a charger.

bring: Your referral and vascular ultrasound results
Documents and a list of your medicines
steps: An IV line is placed, and you lie on the table
The skin in the groin or arm is numbed with a shot
The doctor passes a thin tube into the artery
Contrast dye is injected, and X-rays are taken
If needed, the vessel is widened right away with a balloon or a stent
The tube is removed, and the puncture site is pressed firmly or closed with a special device
feel: A warm feeling in the legs for a few seconds as the dye goes in
Usually no pain from the tube inside the vessel
after: Lie still for a few hours without bending your leg. Your doctor will say how long
Drink more water to help the dye leave your body
No heavy lifting or sports for a few days
A small bruise at the puncture site is common
red_flags: The puncture site swells or bleeds: press on it and call emergency services
The leg turns cold, pale, or numb: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually not. Local numbing is used, sometimes with a sedative.

faq.q: Why can't I bend my leg afterward?
faq.a: So the puncture in the artery seals properly and does not bleed.

reminders.text: Angiogram tomorrow. Pack your documents and test results. Eat only until the time the clinic gave you.
